canonical_statement: There is no total effective Boolean procedure which, for every encoded program and every natural-number input, decides whether the program's universal partial evaluation terminates.

canonical_formal_target.fully_explicit_expression: Not (@ComputablePred.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Code Nat) (@Primcodable.prod.{0, 0} Code Nat (@Primcodable.ofDenumerable.{0} Code Code.instDenumerable) (@Primcodable.ofDenumerable.{0} Nat Denumerable.nat)) Halts)

domain_and_universes: programInput : Nat.Partrec.Code x Nat in universe 0; the target is Prop in universe 0. Every inductive Code is valid and every Nat input, including zero, is included.
ordered_binders: programInput : Nat.Partrec.Code x Nat (implicit universal binder supplied to the predicate)
conclusion: Not (ComputablePred Halts), where Halts programInput is the domain proposition of Nat.Partrec.Code.eval programInput.1 programInput.2.
minimal_import_basis: ComputablePred is defined in Mathlib.Computability.Halting, which publicly imports the universal Code evaluator from PartrecCode. Replacing the direct import by Mathlib.Computability.PartrecCode makes ComputablePred unavailable, so no narrower defining module elaborates this target.
machine_model: Nat.Partrec.Code, mathlib's denumerable inductive syntax for universal partial-recursive programs
halting_predicate: (Nat.Partrec.Code.eval program input).Dom, meaning that universal partial evaluation produces some natural output
decider_contract: ComputablePred Halts: existence of one DecidablePred instance whose Boolean indicator is total and Computable in mathlib's partial-recursive sense
validity_policy: Every Nat.Partrec.Code constructor denotes a program; there is no malformed-code side condition. The pair predicate ranges uniformly over every code and every natural input.

boundary_policy.meaning: Halting is definedness of partial evaluation, not production of a special output, bounded execution, or timeout observation.

source_interpretation: The target-bearing catalog gloss is the standard halting-undecidability family. The repository's fuller computability catalog wording explicitly says that no Turing machine decides whether an arbitrary Turing machine halts on a given input. This statement phase selects the conventional arbitrary-program/arbitrary-input partial-recursive-code realization. It does not claim a source-exact Turing 1936 translation or transfer state from duplicate THM-M-0707.
